missions.title: The Corner House
missions.brief: Every house starts with two shapes: walls with right angles, a roof that must span them exactly. Fit both onto the blueprint.
hints: The dashed outlines show where each piece belongs — start with the big rectangle.
The wall is a rectangle: 4 sides, 4 right angles, opposite sides parallel. It fills the lower outline.
The roof triangle must sit with its base exactly on top of the wall.
missions.reviewNote: Walk the perimeter of the house. Which sides are parallel? Where are the right angles?

missions.title: House With a Wing
missions.brief: A main room, a square wing, one pitched roof and one shed roof. The shed roof may overhang its wall — that is what eaves do.
hints: Build the walls first — the two lower outlines — then find a roof for each.
The square wing carries the trapezoid roof. A trapezoid has exactly ONE pair of parallel sides.
Rotate the trapezoid so its parallel pair runs horizontally: long side at the bottom.
missions.reviewNote: The trapezoid roof has exactly one pair of parallel sides. The walls have two pairs. Count them on the drawing.

missions.title: Lookout Tower
missions.brief: Stack a base, a tall shaft and a watch room, then plant the flag. Watch which sides stay parallel all the way up.
hints: Widest piece at the bottom: the base keeps the tower steady.
The shaft is the tall rectangle — its short sides must line up with the base's top.
The flag is a right triangle — its vertical side glues to the watch room's wall.
missions.reviewNote: Without the flag the tower has a mirror line. The flag breaks it — can you see why?

missions.title: Plank Bridge
missions.brief: One long plank and two piers. The piers must stand plumb — perfectly vertical — or the deck will tilt.
hints: The long plank is the deck — it lies flat across the top.
The piers are bricks standing on end. Rotate a brick 90° so it stands tall.
Each pier slides under the deck at the dashes, one left and one right.
missions.reviewNote: Both piers are the same rectangle. Are their long sides parallel to each other?

missions.title: Mirror Bridge
missions.brief: This bridge must be perfectly symmetric: whatever stands on the left must stand, mirrored, on the right. Both support triangles are congruent.
hints: The deck goes first — flat across the middle dashed outline.
The right support is the left support flipped across the mirror line. Same triangle, mirrored.
Rotate the second triangle 180° so its slope mirrors the first one.
missions.reviewNote: Fold the bridge along the center line in your head: deck, triangles and rails all pair up. That is reflection symmetry.

missions.title: Blocky Bot
missions.brief: Seven pieces, one robot — and every piece must respect the mirror line down its middle.
hints: Body first: the tall rectangle in the middle of the sheet.
Arms are bricks rotated 90° — they hang off the body's sides, level with each other.
Legs sit under the body, one per side of the mirror line. So does everything else.
missions.reviewNote: Blocky Bot is symmetric: arms, legs and rails each have a mirror partner. Trace the mirror line with your eye.

missions.title: Hexapal
missions.brief: A six-sided body on trapezoid feet. Hexagons hide three pairs of parallel sides — count them all.
hints: The hexagon is the body — biggest piece, middle of the sheet.
Feet are trapezoids: rotate so the long parallel side is at the bottom, like a shoe.
The antenna is a small right triangle standing on the body's top edge, tip pointing up-left.
missions.reviewNote: Hexapal's feet each have one pair of parallel sides; its body has three. But the antenna breaks the mirror line — Hexapal is NOT symmetric.

missions.title: Half a House
missions.brief: The architect only drew the left half. Build the right half as its exact mirror image — the mirror line is already on the sheet.
hints: The finished house is symmetric about the dashed mirror line — every printed piece needs a twin.
The roof halves are right triangles. Mirror the left one across the line: rotate it 180°.
Each dashed outline is the same distance from the mirror line as its printed twin.
missions.reviewNote: Every side of the right half matches a side of the left half, the same distance from the mirror line. Same shape, same size, flipped.
